items.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: one of the strongest was Alfred Lion and Frank Wolff with Blue Note. I considered them to be the rock steady client.

ctx.x: The first thing you do is buy property. Elvaho was my wife at the time; she was the scout for property. She went out while I was working and looked for property to build, for her it would be a home, for me it would be a studio. And that’s the way it evolved. That must have been in ’58. She says, “I have a place, come and look at it.” And the place was a piece of property; it was a low, swampy area in Inglewood Cliffs right here. And I said, “I think we can do it there, how much is it?” So she told me the price…
